title: Introduce universal cost-onramp templates and quant safelist adapter
author: Priya Nambiar
description:
This PR adds a declarative onboarding path for cost-optimization defaults (batching/caching presets), a quantization safelist mechanism, and a small CLI to preview tenant unit economics before applying templates. Motivation: customers frequently ask for safe, predictable defaults that can be applied as a single operation during onboarding or for tenant migrations; operators also need a safe way to limit quant profiles to vetted options.

Key components:
- configs/default_onramp_templates.yaml: declarative templates grouping batching shape, cache TTL/policy, and quantization profile references. Templates are idempotent and reference the existing policy DSL.
- pkg/econ/templates.go and pkg/econ/loader.go: loader/validator that expands templates into RuntimeConfig objects and runs lightweight safety checks (latency budget, reserved batch size bounds).
- cmd/costctl: new CLI subcommand 'costctl onramp apply|preview|dryrun' that shows unit-econ impact estimates and writes audit-able changes.
- scripts/quant_safelist_generator.py: tool for maintainers to produce the quant safelist from offline benchmark CSVs; integrates with model-registry metadata.
- migration/migrate_onramp.go: one-off migration that applies a recommended template to tenants marked by Linear ENG-2841.
- docs/costs/onramp.md: operator guide and rollback instructions.

Checklist:
- [x] Add onramp templates and loader
- [x] Implement quant safelist enforcement in runtime config validation
- [x] Build costctl preview and dry-run
- [x] Add unit and e2e tests
- [x] Add docs and changelog entry

Safety model: templates are guarded by a conservative validator with three gates (syntactic, unit-econ threshold, and runtime-safety). Quant safelist enforces that only profiles present in /configs/quant_safelist.csv can be referenced by templates; referencing an unknown profile fails validation. The safelist is intended as a mechanism for staged rollouts and compliance with tenant policies.

Impact: Enables one-click application of a small set of curated defaults during onboarding and reduces manual tuning. The preview CLI provides estimated monthly token cost deltas and expected median latency changes so SREs can make informed decisions.

Related: ENG-2841 (onramp automation), ENG-2967 (quant governance), SUP-9021 (support ticket that motivated default presets).

review_comments: Ethan Park: Left a few nits in templates.go around error wrapping; also question the default cache TTL of 5m for async workloads — can we make that tenant-configurable?
Priya Nambiar: Reply: made TTL tenant-overridable and added a unit test. Kept conservative default of 5m per ENG-2841 guidance.
Nora Wallace: Approve with comments: quant_safelist_generator.py looks fine but add README for maintainers. Also request that CLI output include a JSON machine-readable flag.
Priya Nambiar: Reply: added --json flag to costctl preview and a short maintainer README under scripts/
Diego Alvarez: Requested runtime-safety threshold be tightened; saw a flake in e2e tests on the 99th percentile latencies. Priya adjusted validator and re-ran CI.
release_notes:
- New: declarative cost-onramp templates for batching/caching/quant presets
- New: quant safelist enforcement to limit quant profiles to vetted options
- New: costctl preview/dryrun to estimate tenant unit economics before applying templates
- Docs: operator guide for onramp and rollback
notes: This change was tested against the synthetic-workload lab (benchmark-lab) and a small internal tenant pilot. The quant safelist is seeded from historical benchmark runs; subsequent updates to the safelist will require an attendant compatibility note in the changelog.
